correctness.rationale: The conditional average over relabelings is a five-overlap-type inversion count: probabilities 0,1/3,1,2/3,1/2 yield E[inv|C_1,C_2]=n(n-1)/4+n(1-C_1)/6-C_1(C_1-1)/12+C_2/6. Classical cycle factorial moments then yield covariance -(n+1)/6 at j=1, 1/12 at j=2, 1/6 at j=n, and zero at other j, including n=3 and j=n-1 cancellation. Independently enumerated all permutations n=3..7 to verify the class regression and n=3..6 for cycle-count covariances.

originality.rationale: FAILED by exact earlier general theorem. Axel Hultman, Permutation statistics of products of random permutations (2013 preprint, 2014 journal), Theorem 6.2, gives conjugacy mean of inversions as n(n-1)/4 chi^(n) -(n+1)/6 chi^(n-1,1) -1/6 chi^(n-2,1,1). The elementary identities chi^(n-1,1)=C_1-1 and chi^(n-2,1,1)=binom(C_1-1,2)-C_2 transform it EXACTLY into submitted formula (1) for every n>=3. The covariance entries are routine evaluations via the established cycle factorial moments, with j=2 previously explicitly reported as prior by 2026-11-02 positional-two-cycle work. This is implication coverage despite different character language.
residual_risks: Source differences in notation do not alter decisive character-to-cycle identity.
A complete historical inventory unnecessary to reject: a known earlier theorem already implies submitted principal claim.
